\section{Method}

\subsection{Problem Formulation}
- SwiGLU FFN: y = (σ(xW_g) ⊙ xW_u) W_d, where σ = SiLU
- Gate activation: g = σ(xW_g), g_j determines neuron j's contribution
- Binary mask: m ∈ {0,1}^{d_ff}, applied as y_sparse = (m ⊙ g ⊙ xW_u) W_d
- Goal: learn mask predictor f_θ(h) → s ∈ (0,1)^{d_ff} (soft scores)
- Inference: top-k from s across all layers (TEAL allocation)

\subsection{Predictor Architecture}
- Per-layer lightweight MLP: f_θ^l(h) = σ(hW_1^l)W_2^l
- W_1 ∈ R^{4096×128}, W_2 ∈ R^{128×14336} (2.37M params/layer)
- 32 independent predictors (one per layer), 75.9M total
- Input: hidden state h after attention (before FFN)
- Output: s^l ∈ R^{d_ff}, per-neuron importance scores

\subsection{Gumbel-Sigmoid Relaxation}
- Hard mask m_j = 1[s_j > threshold] is non-differentiable
- Gumbel-Sigmoid: m̃_j = σ((log(s_j/(1-s_j)) + g_1 - g_2) / τ)
  where g_1, g_2 ~ Gumbel(0,1), τ is temperature
- τ annealed from 1.0 to 0.1 during training (cosine schedule)
- Low τ → approaches hard binary mask
- STE baseline comparison: straight-through gradient ∂m/∂s = 1
  → Gumbel contributes 34.5% improvement (PPL 15.77 → 11.79)

\subsection{KL Divergence Training Objective}
- Forward KL: L_KL = KL(p_dense || p_sparse) = Σ_v p_dense(v) log(p_dense(v) / p_sparse(v))
- p_dense = softmax(z_dense / T), p_sparse = softmax(z_sparse / T), T=1
- z_dense from full model, z_sparse from sparse model with mask m̃
- Why forward KL (not reverse): FKL focuses on high-probability tokens,
  preserving the distribution's head — suitable for sparse models that must maintain
  the dense model's primary predictions

\subsection{Lagrangian Sparsity Constraint}
- Constrained optimization: min_θ L_KL  s.t.  (1/L)Σ_l (1/d_ff)Σ_j s_j^l ≤ target
- Lagrangian relaxation: L = L_KL + λ(s̄ - target)
- Dual variable λ updated with gradient ascent: λ ← λ + η_λ(s̄ - target)
- λ automatically increases when sparsity undershoot, decreases when overshoot
- No manual tuning of sparsity-quality tradeoff weight

\subsection{Gradient Analysis: BCE vs KL}
THIS IS THE KEY THEORETICAL SECTION.

BCE loss: L_BCE = -(1/N)Σ_j [m*_j log(s_j) + (1-m*_j)log(1-s_j)]
- Gradient: ∂L_BCE/∂s_j depends only on s_j and m*_j → factorized per neuron
- Each neuron trained independently; no inter-neuron coupling
- m*_j = oracle mask from dense model activation magnitudes

KL loss: L_KL = Σ_v p_dense(v) log(p_dense(v) / p_sparse(v))
- Gradient: ∂L_KL/∂s_j = Σ_v (∂L_KL/∂z_sparse_v)(∂z_sparse_v/∂h)(∂h/∂m̃_j)(∂m̃_j/∂s_j)
- Key: ∂z_sparse/∂h couples all neurons through the output projection W_d
- Changing neuron j's mask affects ALL logits, and KL gradient reflects this
- This is the structural mismatch: BCE optimizes per-neuron accuracy,
  but inference uses global top-k allocation → per-neuron scoring is suboptimal
